name: Blues
description: Delta bottleneck, Chicago electric, and the slow-burning stuff in between: the root system most of this shop grew out of.

name: Classical
description: Symphonies, string quartets and solo piano, pressed for people who want the whole argument rather than the highlights.

name: Electronic
description: From deep house to ambient drift: electronic music for dancing, thinking, or doing both at once.

name: Folk, World, & Country
description: Country twang, front-porch folk, and rhythms from every corner of the map, proof that roots music has no borders.

name: Funk / Soul
description: Rhythm sections that refuse to sit still and voices that carry the room: the good stuff, loud or otherwise.

name: Hip-Hop
description: Breakbeats, boom bap, and everything the sampler made possible once someone thought to loop the good bit.

name: Jazz
description: Modal, cool, hard bop and everything that came after: records for late nights and slow Sundays alike.

name: Latin
description: Salsa, bossa, cumbia and tropicalia: records that assume you have somewhere better to be than sitting down.

name: Pop
description: Hooks built to last three minutes and stay for thirty years, with no apology offered for any of it.

name: Reggae
description: Roots, dub and lovers rock: basslines with room to breathe and mixing desks treated as instruments.

name: Rock
description: Loud guitars, louder hooks, and the odd quiet moment in between: the genre that never really left.

name: Stage & Screen
description: Soundtracks, scores and cast recordings: music written to serve a story that turned out to stand up on its own.
